messages:
dmitri: Heads up — seeing weird sampling hotspot pointing at `mha_fwd` in nsys samples but full timeline doesn't show a long-running kernel there. Suspect sampling bias + KV cache eviction jitter. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

alex: Which nsys command + sample interval did you use? OSRT sampling can bias toward longer kernels, short KV-prefetch bursts often get undersampled.

maria: Also check that you captured `osrt` and `nvtx` ranges. We bracket KV hits/evicts with NVTX so samples can be correlated with trace ranges.

dmitri: Posted the exact command I ran:

```
nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --sample-interval=200us \
  --capture-range=nvtx \
  --capture-range-start=range1:start \
  --capture-range-end=range1:end \
  -o out_kv_bug.qdrep \
  --duration=8s \
  --target-processes=all \
  --force-overwrite
```

alex: Ah, `--sample-interval=200us` is okay but for KV microbursts try 50-100us and shorter bracket windows so the sampler gets a denser picture. Also run multiple brackets (3x) to catch intermittent evict.

sam: Example NVTX bracket pattern we use around the KV hotpath:

```cpp
nvtxRangePushA("kv:prefetch");
// prefetch logic (may be very short)
nvtxRangePop();

nvtxRangePushA("kv:evict");
// eviction heartbeat
nvtxRangePop();
```

maria: If you see a kernel name mismatch between samples and timeline it can be due to kernel variant fallback. Samples latch onto whatever symbol was active when the sample fired, which can look like a long `matmul_q4` even though timeline shows `matmul_fp16` for most of the sequence. We tracked this before by: 1) enabling per-launch annotations, 2) forcing the build to use the same kernel variant to reproduce.

jen: For reproducer I usually do: bracketed captures of 2s with 1s gaps x3, `--sample-interval=75us`, and full `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt`. That combo revealed an intermittent `kv_prefetch` kernel that aligned with CPU eviction threads.

ci-bot: Perf run 2167890123 attached (out_kv_bug.qdrep) — CI job queued to archive artifacts. :robot_face:

alex: A couple tactical checks:
- Try `--sample-interval=50us` to push sampling resolution.
- Try `--sample=osrt` (if available) to bias on OS scheduling jitter.
- Increase `--duration` to 12s if your workload has longer tails.
- Use `nsys stats -r all out_kv_bug.qdrep` and `nsys export` to CSV for quick grep.

maria: Also examine host-side thread names and CPU offload: use `--target-threads=all` so you can see the eviction heartbeat thread names in the timeline. Host thread naming made a huge difference for us when correlating samples to the right actor.

dmitri: Quick follow-up: I ran 3x bracketed captures after Alex's tip and saw the sampler still flagged `mha_fwd` but when I opened the full timeline the heavy work was actually `kv_prefetch` + a micro `layernorm` that immediately triggered a kernel selection fallback. So sampler was attributing to a transient symbol.

sam: That fits the pattern: sampler catches a transient compile/jit path or short fallback. Two general mitigations we've used:
1) bracket and short-capture multiples to increase probability of catching the real hotspot in timeline.
2) temporarily force single kernel variant via env var (e.g., `RW_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_fp16`) so sampling/timeline names match.

jen: Another trick: insert a 1-2ms busywait in the KV prefetch path when running perf debug builds — makes the kernel stable enough to show on both sampler and full trace (only for dev runs).

dmitri: Good notes. I'll:
- re-run 3x 2s brackets with `--sample-interval=50us`, `--target-threads=all`
- force kernel variant to eliminate fallback noise
- attach qdrep + CSV outputs here

alex: One last piece — if you still see mismatches, try a contiguous long capture (`--duration=20s`) with `--capture-range=process` so nvtx ranges are less likely to split the samples. Sometimes splitting brackets correlates poorly with OSRT sampling windows.

maria: TL;DR: sampling bias + kernel fallback + KV eviction heartbeat are a common triplet. Bracketed captures + tighter sample interval + thread visibility usually resolves it. :white_check_mark:

dmitri: Perfect — I'll post results and qdrep links once done. Thanks all. :pray:
